statement_summary: The company must maintain one security program covering enterprise IT, the CCC, plant OT, and product security
Written designations: HIPAA security official for the CCC (IT Director), 524B owner (VP QA/RA), PSIRT lead (Product Security Manager)
Annual SP 800-30 enterprise risk assessment; product cybersecurity risk assessments per release and per new vulnerability, reconciled quarterly
Risk acceptance authority by level; no patient-safety risk accepted above Low
SPDF applies to devices and related systems, including production software that loads firmware, sets device state, or issues identities
SBOM for every release; daily monitoring including KEV; triage service levels; justified regular patch cycle and out-of-cycle path
Published CVD policy; acknowledge within 3 business days; screen as possible complaint; active ISAO membership
Quarterly vCISO report to the audit committee including product security metrics
Security policies must be reviewed at least annually and after major changes or incidents
Written, risk-rated, time-limited exceptions; none may waive a legal requirement
Sanctions proportionate to intent and harm, documented
No PHI without a subcontractor BAA; tiered supplier security review; vulnerability notification terms for critical software suppliers
Security controls must be independently evaluated at least annually (P07) and after major changes
Retention: security, CVD, and PSIRT records 6 years; 806.20 records 2 years beyond device life
AI tools, and AI functions in products or quality processes, must be approved through the AI governance process before use (STD-05; P10)
Unique identity for every user; badge-based individual login on plant stations by 2027-03-31
Owner-approved, least-privilege, role-based access
MFA for all workforce; phishing-resistant MFA for administrators
Just-in-time privileged access to CCC production, signing, and identity; no standing all-tenant write access after 2026-12-31
Quarterly access reviews for CCC, landing zone, repositories, signing service, PLM, eQMS, and MES
Same-day termination; prior roles removed within 5 business days of transfer
Two-person release signing; separation of author, approver, and signer; second reviewer for station software
Vendor and remote admin access only through the broker, approved and recorded; no persistent vendor VPNs into OT
No shared, default, or hardcoded device credentials; service and factory modes disabled before shipment and verified at final test
Unique device certificates; yearly rotation of VM-5 per-hospital keys
Break-glass accounts sealed and tested quarterly
Passwords and other authenticators must meet STD-06
Incident plan and runbooks for an exploited device vulnerability and plant OT ransomware
Report suspected incidents, including unusual device behavior at hospitals, within 1 hour
Log every incident with discovery date and, for products, the date the company learned of the vulnerability
One severity scale; SEV-1 activates the crisis management team within 2 hours
Every product security incident screened as a complaint and for MDR and 806 decisions, documented in the eQMS
Uncontrolled risk: 30-day customer communication, 60-day fix, ISAO share, day-50 checkpoint, 806.10 fallback
regulatory_driver: N31-33-R05 (524B(b)(2)(B)); 21 CFR 806.10; FDA postmarket guidance (2016) section VII.B

statement_summary: Breach decision with documented assessment; notice to hospitals by the shortest BAA, state, or HIPAA clock
regulatory_driver: N62-R03 (164.402; 164.410); state third-party agent notice laws (Fla. Stat. 501.171(6))

statement_summary: The cyber insurer must be notified through its hotline before incident response vendors are engaged
No ransom without CEO, General Counsel, insurer, OFAC check, and law enforcement report
Plant Manager decides line shutdown and lot holds; no release until device history records are verified
Annual exercise per runbook, including a combined product and breach tabletop with counsel
Lessons learned within 30 days; CAPA for product incidents
Every information asset must have an owner and a classification recorded in the asset inventory or document system
Encrypt Restricted data at rest and in transit with company-managed keys
Signing and certificate authority keys only in the HSM under dual control; no software-held issuing keys after 2026-12-31
PHI stays in CCC production; not in non-production or with vendors lacking a BAA
Unfixed vulnerability details handled only in the PSIRT workspace until the disclosure date
Sanitize and record disposal or reuse of media, endpoints, and returned devices
Keep records per the retention schedule, then dispose securely
Restricted and Confidential data must not be entered into AI tools that are not on the approved list (STD-05)
Authorized business use; annual acknowledgment
Report phishing, lost devices, and unusual system or device behavior immediately
Plant floor: no personal devices or USB media; individual operator logins
Approved software only; do not disable security tools
Lock screens; company-managed encrypted laptops only
Send PHI and Confidential data only through approved, encrypted channels to approved recipients
Remote access only from company devices with MFA
Approved AI tools only; no code, PHI, keys, or unfixed vulnerability details in public AI; review AI output
Company systems are monitored for security
